name: Just For Fun

pitch_detail.notes: Small holds through a short bulge ease to easier ground and a chain anchor.

descent_text: Single pitch, 40 ft; well within a 60m rope.
approach: The Dikes sit in the Umatilla National Forest's Walla Walla Ranger District, in the East Fork Touchet River valley near Ski Bluewood, southeast Washington — not near the Snake River. Access is via North Touchet Road out of Dayton, WA, paved for roughly the first 15-16 miles before becoming gravel Forest Service Road 64 at the forest boundary; the road continues to Ski Bluewood and stays in use through winter, but snow on the crags and approach slopes keeps the climbing season to roughly May-October, sometimes from April. Approaches are very short and roadside: the south Megadike is reached by parking near a bridge 1.2 miles past the Middle Point Ridge Trailhead and scrambling directly up the steep hillside above the bridge abutment, while Weeping Wall and Joe's Rock are similar short pullout-to-cliff scrambles at 1.1 and 2.0 miles past the same trailhead respectively. The area is lightly visited and faint-trailed, and the basalt is notably loose/fractured, requiring routine loose-rock cleaning. This route is on the Minidike: park 1.5 miles past the Middle Point Ridge Trailhead on the left (SE) side of the road, just after crossing a bridge over the river. Cross the road, scramble down the bridge abutment, and follow a trail downstream on the NW side.
overview: Easy bolted introduction route off the trail past the break in the Minidike.
beta: Small holds lead through a little bulge to easier 5.2 ground and the chain anchor.
